# vk v0.7.0

Date: 2026-10-29. Status: Experimental development release.
Cargo package: `vkrust` version `0.7.0+1.4.365`. Rust library/import: `vk`. License: MIT.

## Scope

An integrated Rust-native allocator, derived from pinned VMA 3.4.0 algorithms
and behavior, joins the Vulkan bindings and cached loader. Its broad service
surface is implemented; full VMA equivalence and production/performance
qualification remain open. The registry snapshot and generated construction
coverage are unchanged: 842 selected commands, all 234 core Vulkan 1.0–1.4
commands, and construction for all 1,552 concrete records/unions.

## Allocator API

The canonical namespace is `vk::mem`. Principal root types such as `Allocator`,
`Allocation`, `Pool` and `SynchronizedAllocator` re-export their single owners.
Use `use vk::mem as vma` for a caller-local alias. No second crate or C++ bridge
is needed. Allocator free functions and methods share one canonical operation:
`vk::mem::create_buffer_with_options(&mut allocator, &info, &options)` and
`allocator.create_buffer_with_options(&info, &options)` have the same behavior.
Native `vk::create_buffer` remains a distinct unbound-resource operation.

Implemented services include:

- Managed buffers/non-disjoint images, existing-resource allocation and binding,
  mixed granularity packing, automatic/default storage and custom TLSF/linear pools.
- Usage-based memory preferences, explicit/cached budgets and local limits,
  dedication/alignment, trimming, aliasing and core/KHR address admission.
- Counted/persistent mapping, cache/batch/copy helpers, statistics/JSON,
  names/user data, debug guards/fill, native and CPU allocation callbacks.
- Borrowed allocation chains, external import/export configuration, explicit
  platform backing accounting and raw disjoint-plane bindings.
- Explicit Fast/Balanced/Full/Extensive relocation contexts with interruption,
  pinned/ignored state, mapped/raw/alias-group moves and explicit commit/abort.
- Opt-in serialized access and borrowed parallel custom-pool, default-memory-type
  and distinct-backing-block phases, with in-flight reservations and lossless
  restoration on unwind.

Native cleanup, GPU completion, relocation copies and resource/descriptor
replacement stay explicit. Ordinary `Allocator` remains non-Send/non-Sync.

## Compatibility and migration

```toml
[dependencies]
vk = { package = "vkrust", version = "0.7", features = ["allocator"] }
```

Replace `vk::memory` imports with `vk::mem`. Root principal type names stay the
same. Source and tests use `src/rs/mem.rs`, `src/rs/mem/`, `test/rs/test_mem.rs`
and `test/rs/mem/`; the Cargo integration target is `mem`. Public software Vulkan
CI, archive audits and donor fixture paths follow those owners. LLVM/Clang and
Rust 1.98.1 remain the development baseline. Consumers need neither a Vulkan SDK
nor a C/C++ compiler. The default feature is `loader`; `allocator` is opt-in.
The Vulkan metadata suffix identifies generated headers, not a required driver.
`AllocationPolicy::Separate` remains the default; opt into `Automatic` for
heap-sized default pooling, or select a custom pool explicitly.

## Verification and limits

The source checkpoint passes 3,424 workspace tests/doctests and 48 Python tool
checks, strict Clippy, minimal/default configurations, deterministic generation,
rustdoc and native-name search. Pinned-header checks cover 1,447 records, 9,267
layout/value comparisons, 348 bitfield comparisons, all 842 Rust PFNs and 775 C
prototypes. The 67 protected C prototypes remain unqualified. Feature capture
passes 5,752 independent bit-plane comparisons over 279 feature records.

Pinned VMA comparisons pass 1,024 native-model traces / 756,000 operations,
56 virtual traces / 112,344 operations and 1,600 memory-preference cases. The
C++ oracle runs under ASan/UBSan without diagnostics. These are selected synthetic
PFN policies with independent placement/accounting models, not full service
coverage or physical-device evidence. Scoped donor discrepancies remain explicit.

Rust ASan passes all 276 library tests; TSan passes 12 focused threading tests
with a rebuilt instrumented standard library. Neither instruments OS/driver
libraries. Four concurrency and three external-memory profiles pass separate
core/thread-safety and synchronization/thread-safety validation on the recorded
Linux Haswell Vulkan 1.2 driver, without skips or validation errors. The image
profile explicitly submits layout transitions. Windows GNU all-target/all-feature
strict Clippy passes; this is not native Windows execution. Host allocation
fault tests initialize their fixture's lazy pthread mutex before fault injection,
so platform runtime initialization is distinct from allocator metadata work.

The public workflow independently gates the exact sanitized commit, actual
archive consumers, Linux checks, Windows/macOS host tests, pinned header/VMA
oracles and explicit Lavapipe tests. Consult the actual workflow and attached
package proof for their release-specific outcomes. Source test totals alone do
not establish successful registry publication.

Full VMA equivalence remains open: unrestricted mixed placement/mapping phases,
broader donor service and concurrent stress coverage, native platform execution
beyond scoped Linux profiles, complete native relocation-copy qualification,
and comparative performance remain unqualified. Existing Haswell Vulkan 1.2
execution does not qualify physical 1.3/1.4, WSI, video, ray tracing, non-coherent
or positive BDA/device-group hardware. See [qualification](../qualification.md).

## Distribution

Private/public histories use distinct commit IDs, with aligned `v0.7.0` tags.
Public snapshots omit private history, engineering documents and agent/editor
configuration. The release workflow publishes the verified crate and attaches
rustdoc, checksums and build evidence to the GitHub development release.
Published tags and registry versions remain immutable.
